input: Organize a family reunion for this summer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The size and scope of the reunion (immediate family vs. extended family, casual backyard gathering vs. multi-day event) fundamentally changes the complexity of the plan.
Knowing how many people are invited and their demographics (ages, family branches) determines venue capacity, activity choices, and catering needs.
The specific date and location (someone's home, a rented venue, a park) shapes availability, travel logistics, and what can realistically be arranged.
The total budget is one of the most limiting factors — it dictates venue type, catering, activities, and how costs are shared among family members.
Understanding who is organizing and coordinating (one person, a committee, shared responsibility) determines how tasks should be divided and communicated.
The desired style and tone — relaxed vs. structured, food-focused vs. activity-focused — shapes the entire event program and atmosphere.
Knowing what a successful reunion looks like (everyone attending, a specific activity happening, reconnecting with distant relatives) helps prioritize the most important elements of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Organize a Summer Family Reunion Event
gold.taskDescription: Plan and coordinate a family reunion to take place this summer, covering all logistics from venue to activities.

questions.title: How many people are you expecting to attend?
questions.description: Determine the estimated headcount to size the venue, catering, and activities appropriately.

questions.title: Is this immediate family only or extended family too?
questions.description: Clarify the scope of who is included — close household members, cousins, multiple family branches — to define invitations and coordination complexity.

questions.title: Do you have a venue or location already in mind?
questions.description: Identify whether a location has been considered (backyard, park, rented hall, resort) to assess what needs to be researched or booked.

questions.title: What is the overall budget for the reunion?
questions.description: Establish a financial ceiling to guide all spending decisions, from venue to food to entertainment.

questions.title: Are you planning this alone or with a group?
questions.description: Determine whether one person is coordinating everything or if there is a committee sharing responsibilities, which affects how the task plan is structured.

questions.title: What vibe do you want — relaxed hangout or structured activities?
questions.description: Understand the preferred tone and format of the event to shape the program, from open barbecues to organized games or ceremonies.

questions.title: What would make this reunion feel like a true success?
questions.description: Identify the one or two outcomes that matter most — full attendance, a meaningful moment, a specific tradition — to prioritize the right elements of the plan.
